passage:
Monday: At recess Asif opened his tiffin. Kishore, who sat beside him, had forgotten his, so Asif split his parathas without being asked and took the smaller piece himself.
Saturday: Abba said the whole family would go to Dadi's for lunch. Asif had wanted to watch his cricket team practise. He only said, "Okay, I'll get my shoes."
Wednesday: On the walk home, Kishore asked, "Did you really want to go to Dadi's?" Asif kicked a stone. "I liked the biryani. But I also wanted cricket." He smiled. "Next Saturday I'll say it. Abba will listen."

qa.q: What did Asif split with Kishore at recess?
qa.a: Asif split his parathas with Kishore.

qa.q: What was Asif feeling when he said only 'Okay, I'll get my shoes'?
qa.a: He felt a mix of belonging and quiet disappointment: he wanted to watch cricket but went along with the family's plan without saying so.

qa.q: What could Asif do next Saturday so his wish is heard too?
qa.a: He could tell Abba plainly that he would like to watch cricket, as he says he will, while still joining family plans he enjoys.

qa.q: Why might Kishore have asked whether Asif really wanted to go to Dadi's?
qa.a: Kishore had been helped by Asif's kindness and may have noticed how quickly Asif gave in, so a classmate was checking in on Asif's own wish.

grounding: A child in a collective family shares a tiffin and defers to the family's wish without being asked, leaving his own preference unspoken.

passage: You ask why I say "whatever the family wants" so fast? Let me tell you. My name is Sudha, and when I was nine I had a drawing chosen for the school fair on Sunday. But Mama announced that we would all travel to my uncle's house for a naming ceremony that day. Nobody asked me anything, and I said, "Yes, Mama," before anyone could. It felt warm, all of us squeezed on the train with steel boxes of puri. But I kept looking at my drawing inside my bag. Uma, my little sister, slipped her hand into mine without a word. Next year I said aloud, "Mama, my drawing is in the fair." She moved the trip by a day.

qa.q: What was chosen for the school fair on Sunday?
qa.a: A drawing of Sudha's was chosen for the school fair.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling on the train while looking at the drawing?
qa.a: Sudha felt warm belonging with the family but also a quiet sadness about missing the fair, since Sudha kept looking at the drawing.

qa.q: What choice inside the story changed the outcome the next year?
qa.a: Sudha said aloud that the drawing was in the fair instead of silently going along, and Mama moved the trip by a day.

qa.q: What might Uma have understood when she slipped her hand into Sudha's?
qa.a: Uma probably noticed the longing in Sudha's looks at the bag and wanted to comfort Sudha without making a fuss, though the passage does not say what Uma thought.

grounding: A child in a collective culture defers to the family's plan without being asked, and the own preference goes unspoken until later.
